docs.title: comRAD
docs.text:
Your companion for low-coverage RADseq population genomics.

comRAD takes reference-mapped RADseq data, built for 2bRAD, from raw reads to clones, population structure, lineages, kinship, diversity and FST, with demographic models as an extra. It runs on a SLURM cluster as three pipelines that submit and watch their own jobs, and it stops to ask you only where a person should decide.

It is built for corals and other host/symbiont systems: reads are mapped to the host and to a symbiont metagenome and split between them. Leave the symbiont genome out and it runs host only.

docs.title: Why comRAD
docs.text:
Low-coverage RADseq analyses are long chains of tools (ANGSD, PCAngsd, NGSadmix, evalAdmix, NGSremix, realSFS, moments) joined by many small decisions: filters, thresholds, sample lists, what to drop and why. Done by hand, those decisions end up scattered across notebooks and job scripts. comRAD puts them in one config file per analysis, runs the chain the same way every time, and keeps a record of what it did.

  • Genotype likelihoods throughout. Every step works from ANGSD genotype likelihoods, so low depth per sample is handled rather than filtered away. Only per-individual heterozygosity uses a depth floor.
  • Clones from genotypes, not just reads. Clones are called from genotype distance when coverage allows and from IBS when it doesn't, with the cut set by your technical replicates. This separates clones from close relatives even in highly heterozygous species (why).
  • Decisions stay with you. The run pauses at the clone dendrogram and at K, with the evidence laid out. You answer in the config, so the answer is recorded.
  • Checks built in. Technical replicates calibrate and test the clone threshold; a neutral, kin-free rerun checks the lineage calls; heterozygosity is tested against coverage; spectra and models are checked for convergence. Problems that don't stop the run become warnings.
  • Plots at every step. Each step draws quick-look plots (PCA, admixture for every K, kinship, outlier scans, FST, diversity) in your own colours and order, collected in an HTML report.
  • A record of the run. A diary of every step with the numbers for your methods, the versions of every tool, every setting in effect, and an HTML report.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph reads["reads (project folder)"]
    direction TB
    r1[raw pools] --> r2[demultiplex<br>deduplicate] --> r3[rename] --> r4[split by species]
  end
  subgraph popgen["popgen (species folder)"]
    direction TB
    p1[quality filter<br>map host + symbiont] --> p2[coverage QC] --> p3{{clones}}
    p3 --> p4[genotype likelihoods] --> p5{{K}}
    p5 --> p6[lineages, kin<br>outliers] --> p7[SFS: FST, θ,<br>heterozygosity]
  end
  subgraph demo["demography"]
    direction TB
    d1[bootstrap SFS] --> d2[moments models] --> d3[model table]
  end
  reads --> popgen --> demo

The two hexagons are the pauses where you decide.

Each pipeline is a fixed list of steps. comrad run submits one small driver job that runs them in order; each step builds a list of jobs and hands it to comrad-jobs, which submits them as a SLURM job array, reruns only what fails (with more memory, on the long partition, or on another node, as the failure needs), and records what each job used. Run it again after a pause or a stop and it carries on from where it was.

pipeline run from does ends with reads project folder download, demultiplex and deduplicate, rename, split by species <species>/demuxReads/*.demux.fastq.gz popgen species folder QC, mapping, clones, genotyping, structure, K, kin, lineages, outliers, SFS, FST, diversity <SP>Results.tar.gz demography species folder, after popgen contig-bootstrap spectra, moments models, model table and checks <SP>Demography.tar.gz

docs.title: Renamed from radTools
docs.text: comRAD was radTools before its first release. The commands are now comrad (was radpipe.py) and comrad-jobs (was rtjobs.py); the old names are still installed and do the same thing. Configs, .rtjobs/ stamps and run folders are unchanged, so a run started under radTools carries on under comRAD. Older settings are read under their new names, and comrad check says which to rename.

docs.title: Tests and development
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/RyanEckert/comRAD.git && cd comRAD
python3 -m pip install --user .        # after editing a script in scripts/, install again
bash tests/run_mock.sh                 # reads -> popgen -> demography against stand-ins for every tool
bash tests/sim_clones.sh               # the clone call on simulated pedigrees, against the truth
bash tests/check_scripts.sh            # every script is listed, installed and executable
python3 tools/makeDocs.py --check      # the generated reference pages are up to date

tests/run_mock.sh checks the wiring between steps (tests/fake.py stands in for each tool), including the pauses, kin drop, outliers, the host-only path and K = 1. It does not test the tools themselves. Variants: MOCK_HOSTONLY=1, MOCK_K=1, MOCK_METRIC=geno, MOCK_OLDKEYS=1. tests/sim_clones.sh simulates clones, replicates and relatives at about 7x and 2.5x and checks which are grouped.

The documentation site is built with MkDocs Material: pip install mkdocs-material then mkdocs serve in the repository folder.

docs.title: Install
docs.text: comRAD needs a Linux cluster with SLURM and Python 3.9 or newer. Installing it is two steps: comRAD itself with pip, then the external programs it runs with comrad setup.

docs.title: 1. comRAD
docs.text:
module load python                 # whichever Python you will run with (if your cluster uses modules)
python3 -m pip install --user git+https://github.com/RyanEckert/comRAD.git
comrad -h

This installs comrad, comrad-jobs, every script the pipelines call, and the Python packages they use (numpy, scipy, matplotlib, moments, demes, PCAngsd and cutadapt). R is not needed.

Small home folder?

pip --user installs into ~/.local. To put it on bigger storage instead, set PYTHONUSERBASE before installing, and put its bin on your PATH:

echo 'export PYTHONUSERBASE=/path/to/storage/.local' >> ~/.bashrc
echo 'export PATH=$PYTHONUSERBASE/bin:$PATH' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Load the same Python before installing that you will run comRAD with: pip writes that interpreter into each script's first line. If pip itself is missing, python3 -m ensurepip --upgrade --user installs it. To update comRAD later, run the same pip install with --upgrade; to install a tagged version, add @v0.1.0 after .git.

docs.title: 2. The programs comRAD runs
docs.text:
comrad setup --prefix /path/to/storage/comradDeps
echo 'source /path/to/storage/comradDeps/comrad.env' >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

Below, DIR is that --prefix folder; put it on storage with space, not a small home folder. For each program that is not already on your PATH, comrad setup tries, in order:

  1. an environment module (module avail); comrad.env loads the ones it finds;
  2. conda/mamba from bioconda, into DIR/conda. With no conda or mamba on the cluster, it first installs Miniforge into DIR/miniforge (no admin rights needed); --no-conda skips conda altogether;
  3. a download or build from source in DIR/src (needs git, make and a C/C++ compiler);
  4. pip, for the Python tools.

Everything it installs is linked into DIR/bin, which comrad.env puts on your PATH. Anything it could not install, it prints the steps for; they are also below. comrad check popgen (in a species folder) lists anything still missing.

This page is written by comrad setup --write-docs docs/install.md, from the same list setup uses.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: One project, from raw reads to results. Every command runs on the cluster's login node; comRAD submits its own jobs. Each step is explained in the guide.

docs.title: Once per cluster
docs.text:
python3 -m pip install --user git+https://github.com/RyanEckert/comRAD.git
comrad setup --prefix /path/to/storage/comradDeps          # finds or installs ANGSD, bowtie2, ...
echo 'source /path/to/storage/comradDeps/comrad.env' >> ~/.bashrc && source ~/.bashrc

Index each reference genome once:

bowtie2-build sintGenome.fa sintGenome.fa && samtools faidx sintGenome.fa

docs.title: Once per project
docs.text:
cd /path/to/myProject                # rawReads/, sampleID.csv and metadata.csv go here
comrad init cluster                  # partitions, largest node memory, email
nano cluster.config

docs.title: Reads: raw pools to one file per sample
docs.text:
comrad init reads && nano reads.config      # SAMPLE_SHEET, SPECIES
comrad check reads
comrad run reads
comrad status reads                         # where it is, or why it stopped

docs.title: Popgen: one species
docs.text:
cd sint
comrad init popgen && nano popgen.config    # SP, GENOME_FASTA, META, TECHREPS, ...
comrad check popgen
comrad run popgen
comrad summary popgen                       # what each step found so far, and what waits on you

It pauses twice. (Set CLONE_PAUSE = no and K in the config beforehand and it never does.) First at the clone dendrogram:

comrad status popgen                        # the last line says what to look at
nano popgen.config                          # CLONE_PAUSE = no  (accept)  or  CLONE_CUT = 0.08  (your own)
comrad run popgen

Then at K:

less run/popgen/K.log                       # the reads on K, side by side
# and the plots: pcangsd/sintPca.pdf, ngsAdmix/sintAdmix.pdf, ngsAdmix/sintResiduals.pdf
nano popgen.config                          # K = 2
comrad run popgen

When it finishes, sintResults.tar.gz holds the results and run/popgen/popgenReport.html summarises the run, warnings first.

docs.title: Demography (optional)
docs.text:
comrad init demography && nano demography.config   # SP, MU
comrad run demography

docs.title: Finding out why it stopped
docs.text:
comrad status popgen                 # the last events; the reason for a pause or stop is the last line
comrad summary popgen                # each step's notes and warnings from its last run, and any open pause or stop
less run/popgen/<step>.log           # the step's full output
ls -t <folder>/<jobname>*.e* | head  # the jobs' own error logs, next to their outputs

From a project folder, comrad summary popgen --dir sp1 sp2 sp3 does several species at once.

A pause is a decision for you (the clone dendrogram, K); a stop is something a rerun on its own will not fix. In both cases the message says what to look at. Fix it, then comrad run popgen carries on from the step that stopped.

comrad-jobs has already retried failed jobs before a step stops: on long_queue after a time limit, with double the memory (up to max_mem) after running out, on another node after a node failure, and once more for anything else. A stop means that wasn't enough.

docs.title: Rerunning after a fix
docs.text:
you want to command carry on after a stop or pause comrad run popgen redo from a step because its inputs or settings changed comrad from popgen <step> start at a step when earlier ones were done by hand comrad from popgen <step> --mark-earlier run one step now, in this shell comrad step popgen <step>

run does not notice a setting you changed for a step that is already done: use from. Deleting an output folder by hand (for example angsd/) also needs a from at the step that makes it; the depth step remakes the bam lists if angsd/ is gone.

docs.title: Cluster problems
docs.text:
• The driver waits in the queue for a long time. A driver with no time limit can sit behind other jobs; set driver_time in cluster.config (or comrad run popgen -t 2-00:00:00). If it runs out, comrad run popgen picks up at the step it was in.
  • sacct did not answer in the job notes: peak memory is not recorded, nothing else is affected.
  • bgzf errors from ANGSD or realSFS on parallel file systems (BeeGFS), e.g. Failed to read BGZF header then safreader.cpp ... Assertion failed (exit 134), on files that pass gzip -t. The genotype step copies the bams to node-local disk first. Every realSFS and thetaStat call goes through localSaf.py, which fails (exit 75, so the job is retried) on any bgzf message instead of keeping a partial result. If the errors persist, set local_copy = yes in cluster.config: realSFS and thetaStat then read copies of their SAF, theta and FST files on node-local disk ($TMPDIR), which needs space for the largest SAF.
  • Moving a species folder while its driver runs breaks the run (paths are absolute); move it between runs.

docs.title: Tutorial: from raw 2bRAD reads to lineages, FST and demography
docs.text:
This walks through one project from start to finish: raw pool fastqs from one sequencing run holding two coral species, through lineages, diversity and FST, to moments demographic models. Every command is run on the cluster's login node; comrad submits its own jobs.

The example files are in the repository's examples/ folder: cluster.config, reads.config, popgen.config, demography.config, sampleID.csv, metadata.csv. The guide explains each stage in more depth; this page is the path through it.

docs.title: 1. What you need
docs.text:
Software (comrad check <pipeline> lists anything missing):

  • SLURM (job arrays; nothing else needed for submitting)
  • ANGSD (with realSFS, thetaStat), bowtie2, samtools
  • NGSadmix, evalAdmix, NGSremix, ngsParalog (PCAngsd and cutadapt install with comRAD)
  • Python 3.9+ (comRAD installs the Python packages it needs; R is not needed)

The examples keep everything under one storage folder exported as $koko; any exported variable works in a config path, or none.

Install comRAD (straight from GitHub; pip puts the commands in ~/.local/bin):

python3 -m pip install --user git+https://github.com/RyanEckert/comRAD.git
comrad -h

Load the Python module you will run with before installing: pip writes that interpreter into every script it installs.

Install the other tools: comrad setup checks for each one and, for any that is missing, looks for an environment module, then uses conda/mamba (with no conda on the cluster, it installs Miniforge into the folder first; --no-conda skips that), then downloads or builds it from source (pip for the Python tools). It installs into the folder you give it, never your home folder, and prints the manual steps for anything it could not install (docs/install.md has the same list).

comrad setup --prefix $koko/bin/comradDeps
echo "source $koko/bin/comradDeps/comrad.env" >> ~/.bashrc    # PATH for what it installed

A module it finds is reported, not loaded: add the module load lines it prints to ~/.bashrc (they are also in comrad.env).

Cluster settings, once per project: partitions, the largest node's memory, email and any extra sbatch flags your cluster needs (an account, a constraint).

cd $koko/2bRAD/myProject
comrad init cluster && nano cluster.config      # see examples/cluster.config

Every pipeline run in that folder, or up to three folders below it, reads it. On a busy partition a driver with no time limit can wait behind other jobs; driver_time = 2-00:00:00 (or comrad run popgen -t 2-00:00:00) can let it start sooner. If it runs out, comrad run popgen picks up at the step it was in.

Genomes: indexed once, beforehand.

bowtie2-build sintGenome.fa sintGenome.fa && samtools faidx sintGenome.fa

docs.title: 2. Inputs
docs.text:
file what it holds rawReads/<pool>.fastq.gz one fastq per pool (i7/i5 index), named by pool; trim2bRAD.py names each library <pool>_<barcode> from it sampleID.csv pool_barcode,sample per line, no header. Technical replicates are <sample>.1, .2, .3; the original library is always .1 metadata.csv one row per sample, replicates included; a sample column plus whatever you group by (bank, depthZone, ...)

The sample-name prefix decides the species (SGM = sint, PGM = past, set in SPECIES). Every sample that ends up with reads must have a metadata row: comrad check popgen stops and lists any that don't.

myProject/                    cluster.config  reads.config  sampleID.csv  metadata.csv  rawReads/
  sint/                       popgen.config  demography.config
    demuxReads/ filteredReads/ bams/ angsd/ pcangsd/ ngsAdmix/ relatedness/ sfs/ het/ theta/ demo/
    run/popgen/               one .log and .done per step, popgenSummary.txt (the diary), versions.txt, settings copies
  past/                       ...

docs.title: 3. Reads: trim, demultiplex, rename, split by species
docs.text:
cd $koko/2bRAD/myProject
comrad init reads           # or: cp $koko/bin/comRAD/examples/reads.config .
nano reads.config
comrad check reads
comrad run reads
comrad status reads         # last events, and whether the driver is still queued

Steps: download (skipped without BS_PROJECTS), demux, demuxcheck, rename, species. When it finishes, each species folder has demuxReads/*.demux.fastq.gz, one per sample, and rawReads/RawCounts.pdf plots the yield per pool. Check:

cat rawReads/RawCounts                            # raw and kept reads per pool
ls sint/demuxReads/*.demux.fastq.gz | wc -l       # samples per species
ls unassigned/demuxReads/                         # libraries with no sample name: empty wells, barcode errors

A barcode with fewer than 100,000 reads (trim2bRAD.py's default) gets no file, so failed libraries are simply absent. If a sample you expect is missing, find its barcode in rawReads/logs/<pool>.demux.log.

File names along the way: demuxReads/<s>.demux.fastq.gz (demultiplexed, deduplicated) → filteredReads/<s>.filtered.fastq.gz (cutadapt) → filteredReads/<s>.host.bam, <s>.symbiont.bam (bowtie2; removed by clean) → bams/<s>.bam, bams/<s>.sym.bam (after the host/symbiont split). Logs are in each folder's logs/; job lists are <SP><Step>Jobs.

docs.title: 4. Popgen: mapping to lineages, diversity and FST
docs.text:
cd sint
comrad init popgen          # or copy examples/popgen.config and edit it
nano popgen.config
comrad check popgen
comrad run popgen

The steps, in order (comrad list popgen shows which are done):

stage steps reads and mapping cutadapt, readcounts, map (host and symbiont), alignrates, split, clean QC and clones depth, clones, clonegroups (pause 1), filterbams genotypes and structure paralog, genotype, structure, admix, symbionts, K (pause 2) lineages assign, kin, lineagebams, lineagesnps, outliers, neutral statistics sfssites, saf, fst, fstall, groups, het, theta, tarball

docs.title: Leaving analyses out
docs.text:
SKIP lists steps not to run, e.g. SKIP = het theta groups. check says what each one changes, as a note or a WARNING, and stops on a step later ones need (only het theta groups fstall symbionts neutral kin outliers fst can be skipped):

note: SKIP het: no per-individual heterozygosity
WARNING: SKIP kin: related individuals stay in: SFS, theta, Tajima's D and FST will include close kin, ...
WARNING: SKIP outliers: SNPs under selection stay in the SFS and FST: demography assumes neutral sites, ...
WARNING: SKIP fst: no lineage FST, fstall is skipped as well, and the demography pipeline cannot run ...

The same lines go in the diary when the run starts, a skipped step's files are left out of the results tarball, and the demography check repeats the kin and outlier warnings. To run a step you skipped earlier, take it out of SKIP and use comrad from popgen <step>.

docs.title: Pause 1: clones (with CLONE_PAUSE = yes)
docs.text:
CLONE_PAUSE = yes is the default. Samples with almost no data look close to everything and pull the clone groups together, so samples below CLONE_MINQ (default 0.20) of sites at ≥ QDEPTHx (default 5) are left out of the clone step; the diary names them and angsd/clones/sintCloneLowCoverage.txt lists them. They would fall below MINQ (0.25) afterwards in any case. Check that no technical replicate is among them: a replicate left out cannot help set the cut.

With CLONE_METRIC = auto, the clone step measures genotype distance (the share of sites where two samples' confident genotype calls differ) when coverage supports it, and IBS otherwise; the diary and sintCloneMetric.txt say which and why. The cut (CLONE_CUT = auto) comes from the technical replicates: for genotype distance, the bottom of the widest gap just above them; for IBS, their deepest join × TREE_BUFFER (the treeTrimmer method). Clones and K explains both.

The run stops after drawing angsd/sintCloneDend.pdf: the tree, technical replicates in bold, and the cut as a red line. Checks that come with it: sintCloneReplicates.txt gives each replicate's nearest sample, and a replicate whose nearest sample is outside its own clone group gives a WARNING (a mislabelled or failed library); sintCloneBorderline.txt lists joins near the cut with each side's coverage (a weak library on one side points to a clone, good coverage on both to a close relative); and if the clone groups would drop more than CLONE_MAXDROP (0.5) of the samples, the run stops: that is a cut or data problem, not a result.

Look for a gap between the clone-level pairs (replicates and true clones, near the bottom) and everything else. If the red line sits in that gap, accept it; if not, set your own.

nano popgen.config     # accept:  CLONE_PAUSE = no      or set your own:  CLONE_CUT = 0.08
comrad run popgen

If you already trust the clone call (for example on a rerun), set CLONE_PAUSE = no before running and it never stops here.

filterbams then keeps the best-covered sample of each clone group and drops samples below MINQ. genotype warns about samples covering under half the median proportion of SNPs; check where they fall in the PCA.

docs.title: Pause 2: K (with K empty)
docs.text:
Look at pcangsd/sintPca.pdf (the PCA, coloured by your sampling groups) and ngsAdmix/sintAdmix.pdf (admixture bars for every K, one sample order). The diary, and run/popgen/K.log, give five reads on K:

note  K: evalAdmix elbow K = 2 (residual RMSD against K)
note  K: PCAngsd K = 2 (eigenvectors kept by its MAP test + 1; ...)
note  K: residual-block K = 2 (smallest K whose worst cluster-block mean |residual| < 0.01; plots: ngsAdmix/sintResiduals.pdf)
note  K: k-means BIC K = 2 (lowest BIC of k-means on the PCA scores, as adegenet find.clusters; ...)
note  K: runs in the dominant mode per K: 1:20/20 2:20/20 3:18/20 4:9/20
  • evalAdmix elbow: where the residual curve flattens. A geometric heuristic: it always returns something, and is never K = 1 or MAXK.
  • PCAngsd: the number of eigenvectors its MAP test kept, plus one; its own admixture at that K is the bottom row of the admixture plot.
  • k-means BIC: k-means clustering of the PCA scores, the K with the lowest BIC (DAPC's find.clusters). Independent of NGSadmix; like PCAngsd, it also responds to families and batches.
  • Residual-block K: read from the evalAdmix residual heatmaps in ngsAdmix/sintResiduals.pdf. Each sample is placed in its main cluster at MAXK; a K that lumps two real lineages leaves red blocks within them and blue between. It's the smallest K with no block mean above RESID_MAX. It cannot tell you K is too high, and the cut-off is a judgement call: look at the plots.
  • Mode support: how many of the 20 NGSadmix runs agree at each K. Low support means that K is not a stable solution.

Then:

nano popgen.config     # K = 2
comrad run popgen

If you already know K, set it before the run and it never pauses here.

K = 1 (no structure) is allowed: every sample is one lineage, fst and fstall are skipped (FST among sampling groups still runs in groups), and the demography pipeline's check stops, since its models need two lineages. At K ≥ 2, fewer than two lineages with pure individuals still stops at assign.

docs.title: When it finishes
docs.text:
Each step has drawn its quick-look plots along the way (reads, symbionts, PCA, admixture, kinship, outliers, the neutral rerun, FST, heterozygosity, θ), and comrad report popgen gathers them, with the warnings and key tables, into run/popgen/popgenReport.html. Results, plots and the report describes each, and how to set their colours and order.

sintResults.tar.gz holds everything the R side needs:

folder contents . bam lists, lineage calls (BamsClusters), kin table, alignment and retention rates qc depth distributions, per-sample coverage at 3/5/10x clones clone groups, distance used and cut, dendrogram(s), replicate check, borderline joins, samples left out of the clone step structure beagle, PCAngsd covariance and F_IS, best NGSadmix Q per K, evalAdmix fit and residuals, neutral rerun and its comparison with the lineages plots every step's quick-look PDF relatedness NGSremix table diversity heterozygosity (with HetDepth.txt), π/θ/Tajima's D (and the THETA_N subsample lists), FST between lineages and groups, 2D spectra run the diary, popgenReport.html, versions.txt and every copy of the settings

Heterozygosity and coverage. Heterozygosity is estimated per sample on the SFS sites with at least 10 reads in that sample. A sample with less coverage reaches 10x at fewer, and different, sites, so het also tests whether heterozygosity follows coverage (Spearman's ρ against nSites and against the proportion of sites ≥ QDEPTHx, permutation p). The result is het/<SP>HetDepth.txt and a diary note; p < 0.05 gives a WARNING. If it warns, compare groups with coverage as a covariate, or downsample the bams to one depth and rerun het.

θ and sample size. theta/<SP>Theta.out gives π, Watterson's θ, Tajima's D and the number of sites per lineage, from all its pure, kin-free individuals (n). π is the comparison to make between lineages of different size; θ_W and Tajima's D depend on n. With THETA_N set (a number, or min for the smallest lineage) the same statistics are also estimated from that many individuals per lineage, in the Sub columns; the individuals used are listed in theta/sub/ and are the same on every run. Compare θ_W and Tajima's D in those columns when lineage sizes differ much.

Sampling groups. groups keeps lineage × sampling-group combinations with at least MIN_GROUP (default 5) individuals for group FST; the diary names each one left out and its n. Heterozygosity per group is the per-sample het/<SP>.het joined with angsd/<SP>Groups, which the R side does.

docs.title: 5. Demography: moments models between lineages
docs.text:
Run in the same species folder, after popgen has finished:

comrad init demography      # or copy examples/demography.config
nano demography.config
comrad check demography
comrad run demography

For each pair of lineages it builds 100 contig-bootstrap spectra, fits every model in MODELS 50 times (FIT_SEEDS × FIT_RUNS), keeps the best run of each, and ranks them by CLAIC: AIC corrected for linked sites using the bootstrap spectra.

Two checks run automatically:

  • convergence: do the best runs of a model agree?
  • nesting: does every larger model fit at least as well as the smaller model it contains? If not, its optimiser stopped early (demo/nesting.txt).

The result is sintDemography.tar.gz. The model names follow the SI / IM / AM / SC convention with 2m (heterogeneous migration) and 2N (heterogeneous Ne) suffixes; momentsModels.py -h describes each.

docs.title: 6. Rerunning
docs.text:
you want to command carry on after a stop or pause comrad run popgen redo from a step because its inputs or settings changed comrad from popgen <step> start at a step when earlier ones were done by hand comrad from popgen <step> --mark-earlier run one step now, in this shell comrad step popgen <step> see which steps are done comrad list popgen

run skips steps already done, and inside a step skips jobs that already finished. It does not notice files you changed by hand, or a setting used by a step that is already done: that's what from is for. Every job in a rewound step reruns, even where an old output file exists.

Moving a species folder while its driver is running breaks the run (paths are absolute); move it between runs.

docs.title: 7. What gets recorded
docs.text: The diary (run/popgen/popgenSummary.txt) has one line per event and a note with the numbers for your methods at every step; comrad summary popgen prints them step by step. run/popgen/ also keeps the tool versions and a copy of the settings each time they change. Running and rerunning has the details, along with how jobs, logs and memory are handled.

docs.title: 8. When something stops
docs.text:
comrad status popgen              # the reason is the last line
comrad summary popgen             # every step's notes and warnings, and any open pause or stop
less run/popgen/<step>.log        # the step's full output

comrad-jobs has already retried failed jobs (on long_queue after a time limit, with more memory after running out); a stop means that wasn't enough. Troubleshooting lists the usual messages and what to do.

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
Two examples of the clone step, the decision that shapes every analysis after it.

  • Clones in a highly heterozygous coral: real data from four Gulf of Mexico corals, where IBS could not separate clones from relatives in Porites astreoides and genotype distance could. How comRAD came to use genotype distance by default.
  • Clone calls on a simulated pedigree: a simulated population with known clones, replicates and relatives, at good and at low coverage. What each distance and cut gets right and wrong, and how CLONE_METRIC = auto chooses between them.

To run either on your own data, cloneTestRun.py, cloneTestScore.py and simCloneKin.py are installed with comRAD (scripts).

docs.title: Clone calls on a simulated pedigree
docs.text: Real data never tell you which pairs truly are clones. A simulation does. simCloneKin.py builds a population with every kind of pair the clone step has to tell apart, draws reads for each sample at a chosen coverage, and writes the same files ANGSD would (genotype probabilities and an IBS matrix), plus a table of the true relationship of every related pair.

docs.title: The design
docs.text:
Two lineages (FST 0.1), each with:

  • 12 unrelated founders;
  • 4 full-sib families of 3 offspring, with both parents sampled (parent–offspring pairs);
  • 2 half-sib groups;
  • 1 selfed family (a parent and 3 selfed offspring), the closest relatives a clonal coral can have;
  • 4 genets with 1–3 extra clone ramets (with a few somatic mutations);
  • 2 colonies sequenced 3 times as technical replicates;
  • 6 weak samples at about 2x, all clones or replicates of others.

About 125 samples and 8000 SNPs; coverage varies between samples around the median. Three runs:

run command what it adds good coverage simCloneKin.py -o simA median 7x a big heterozygous clone simCloneKin.py -o simP --big-clone 25 --fixed-het 0.3 one genet with 25 ramets and extra heterozygosity, like P. astreoides low coverage simCloneKin.py -o simL --cov 2.5 median 2.5x

Each was scored with cloneGroups.py as the clone step runs it, then compared with the truth (this is tests/sim_clones.sh).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Clone pairs grouped (of all true clone and replicate pairs), and relatives wrongly grouped with them:

run distance cut clone pairs grouped relatives grouped as clones good coverage IBS treeTrimmer 89 / 89 15 parent–offspring, 24 selfed-sib genotypes (0.99) widest gap 89 / 89 none big heterozygous clone IBS treeTrimmer 89 / 389 15 parent–offspring, 24 selfed-sib genotypes (0.95) widest gap 389 / 389 none low coverage IBS treeTrimmer 89 / 89 15 parent–offspring, 24 selfed-sib genotypes (0.95) widest gap 87 / 89 20 parent–offspring, 9 selfed-sib, 2 full-sib, 2 half-sib

Bold rows are what CLONE_METRIC = auto chose.

  • At good coverage, genotype distance is right and IBS is not. IBS finds every clone but also merges parent–offspring pairs and selfed sibs, which share half or more of their alleles.
  • A heterozygous clone breaks IBS. The 25 ramets of the heterozygous genet sit far apart in IBS (each pair of libraries draws different alleles at its many heterozygous sites), well above the cut set by the replicates, so IBS misses 300 of its clone pairs. Genotype distance groups all of them.
  • At low coverage, IBS is the better choice. Too few sites have confident genotype calls in both samples, and genotype distance makes more mistakes. The auto checks detect this (only 29% of pairs share 1000 confident sites at 0.99) and fall back to IBS. IBS still merges close relatives at this coverage, which is why <SP>CloneBorderline.txt lists each join near the cut with both sides' coverage.

docs.title: Every pair, by its true relationship
docs.text:
Each dot is a pair of samples from the run with the big heterozygous clone, placed at its distance and sorted by how the two are truly related; the red line is the cut comRAD chose. A correct call puts every clone pair left of the line and every other pair right of it.

  • IBS (left). The big genet's ramets sit at about 0.24, among the half-sibs and unrelated pairs, far right of the cut: each pair of libraries draws different alleles at its many heterozygous sites. Meanwhile a share of parent–offspring pairs and all selfed sibs sit left of the cut, as close as the replicates.
  • Genotype distance (right). Every clone pair, the big genet included, sits near zero; the closest relatives start above 0.03, and the cut falls in the gap between them.

docs.title: The cuts
docs.text:
Each distance needs its own cut:

  • Genotype distance: the widest gap just above the replicates. Clones and replicates sit near zero and relatives much higher, so the tree has a clear gap. comRAD takes the widest gap whose lower edge is within three times the replicates' largest distance (so it cannot jump to the gap between relatives and unrelated samples) and cuts at its bottom. treeTrimmer would cut too low here: replicates are often tighter than clones that include a weak library.
  • IBS: treeTrimmer. IBS never starts near zero, so there is no gap to find at the bottom of the tree; the replicates' deepest join × TREE_BUFFER is the better rule.

docs.title: Run it yourself
docs.text:
simCloneKin.py -o simTest                     # or with --big-clone, --cov, --fst ...
cd simTest
cloneGroups.py -i cloneTests/base/sim.ibsMat -g cloneTests/base/sim.geno.gz -b simBams \
  -r "$(cat techreps.txt)" -o sim             # what the clone step does
cloneTestScore.py -s sim -r "$(cat techreps.txt)" --truth truth.tsv --plot sim.pdf
                                              # every distance and cut, scored against the truth

On your own data, cloneTestRun.py reruns the clone step's ANGSD with a set of filter variants and cloneTestScore.py compares them, without the truth.

docs.title: Clones in a highly heterozygous coral
docs.text: Four coral species from the northwestern Gulf of Mexico (Montastraea cavernosa, Orbicella faveolata, Stephanocoenia intersepta and Porites astreoides), 2bRAD, mapped to each species' genome. Each had technical replicates: the same colony, sequenced as two or three libraries.

docs.title: What went wrong with IBS
docs.text:
The first clone step used IBS: ANGSD's -doIBS 1, which takes one random read per sample at each site, and the treeTrimmer cut (the replicates' deepest join × TREE_BUFFER). It worked for three species. For P. astreoides (128 samples) it did not:

  • only 4 of 9 replicates had one of their own replicates as their nearest sample;
  • replicates of one colony sat further apart than some unrelated-looking pairs, so no cut could group the replicates without grouping other samples too;
  • the dendrogram had no clean gap between clone-level and other pairs.

Why. With one random read per site, two libraries of the same colony draw different alleles at about half of its heterozygous sites. So the IBS distance between clones is not near zero: it grows with the colony's heterozygosity. In a species with high heterozygosity, clones sit as far apart as close relatives. Filters did not fix it: removing sites with skewed read ratios at heterozygous calls (-hetbias_pval), depth floors, a maximum depth, a flat genotype prior and a lower minor-allele cut-off each left the IBS tree as confused, and the read-ratio filter alone removed 32–58% of sites.

Was the heterozygosity real? Collapsed paralogs (two gene copies mapped as one) also look heterozygous. Here, sites heterozygous in most samples had only 1.14–1.20 times the usual depth (paralogs would show about twice), balanced reference and alternative read counts, and were spread across all 14 chromosomes of the reference (jaPorAstr1). The heterozygosity was real.

docs.title: Genotype distance
docs.text:
Genotype distance asks a different question: at sites where both samples' genotype calls are confident (probability above 0.99), how often do the calls differ? Clones share genotypes, so their distance sits near zero however heterozygous they are; relatives differ at a share of sites set by how related they are. It needs enough coverage for confident calls, which these data had.

With genotype distance at 0.99 and the cut at the widest gap just above the replicates:

species clone groups samples dropped as clones pairs with ≥ 1000 shared sites replicate tightness P. astreoides 19 82 100% 0.064 O. faveolata 13 18 100% 0.086 S. intersepta 9 16 100% 0.122 M. cavernosa 4 5 100% 0.080

Replicate tightness is the replicates' largest distance divided by the median distance between all samples: small means replicates sit far below everything else. The groups barely moved across the filter variants: only a depth floor of 5 reads per sample changed one P. astreoides call (18 groups, 83 dropped). For the three species where IBS worked, genotype distance agreed with it.

Two details from this data set:

  • A weak library joins its clone a little higher. In O. faveolata, OGM009 joined two clone mates at 0.068, above most clone pairs. It had 0.56 of its sites at ≥ 5x against 0.87 and 0.89 for the other two, and shared about half as many confident sites with them. A weak library, not a relative. This is why <SP>CloneBorderline.txt lists each side's coverage.
  • The IBS cut needs its buffer. For O. faveolata, IBS with treeTrimmer grouped correctly only with TREE_BUFFER between 1.05 and 1.15 (1.00 split a replicate pair, 1.20 merged another), hence the default of 1.10.

docs.title: What comRAD does now
docs.text:
• CLONE_METRIC = auto (the default) uses genotype distance when the data support it: at least 90% of pairs share 1000 or more confident sites, and replicate tightness is at most 0.15. It tries 0.99, then 0.95, and otherwise falls back to IBS.
  • CLONE_CUT = auto uses the widest gap above the replicates for genotype distance, and treeTrimmer for IBS.
  • The clone ANGSD run already writes genotype probabilities, so this costs no extra job.
  • <SP>CloneMetric.txt and the diary record the choice and the numbers behind it.

Clone calls on a simulated pedigree tests both choices against a known truth.

docs.title: Clones and K
docs.text: popgen pauses twice, where the right answer depends on your data: the clone threshold and the number of genetic clusters, K. In both cases comRAD lays out the evidence, and you answer in the config, so the decision is recorded with the run. If you already know the answer, put it in the config before running and the pause is skipped.

docs.title: Pause 1: clones
docs.text:
Clonal organisms put several samples of one genotype in a collection. Keeping them all inflates relatedness and skews allele frequencies, so the clonegroups step finds clone groups and filterbams keeps the best-covered sample of each.

Which samples go in. A sample with almost no data looks close to everything in an IBS tree and pulls unrelated samples together. Samples covering less than CLONE_MINQ (0.20) of sites at QDEPTHx (5x) are left out of the clone step. They would fall below MINQ (0.25) afterwards in any case. The diary names them, and angsd/clones/<SP>CloneLowCoverage.txt lists them. Check that none of your technical replicates are among them.

The distance. Two ways to measure how different two samples are:

  • Genotype distance: the share of sites where the two samples' genotype calls differ, among sites both are called at with high confidence (probability above 0.99, or 0.95). Clones and replicates sit near 0, whatever the species' heterozygosity.
  • IBS (1 - IBS): one random read per sample and site. It works at very low coverage, but two libraries of one heterozygous genotype differ at about half its heterozygous sites, so clones of a highly heterozygous species sit far from 0 and close to their relatives.

With CLONE_METRIC = auto (the default) comRAD uses genotype distance when the data support it: at least 90% of pairs share 1000 or more confident sites, and the replicates are tight (their largest distance at most 0.15 of the median distance). It tries 0.99, then 0.95, and otherwise uses IBS. The diary and <SP>CloneMetric.txt give the numbers behind the choice. geno or ibs forces one; both uses genotypes and also writes the IBS tree, with the pairs the two group differently.

In simulations with clones, replicates, parents and offspring, full, half and selfed sibs at about 7x, genotype distance found every clone with no relative merged, including a large clone of a highly heterozygous genet; IBS merged parent-offspring and selfed-sib pairs and missed that clone. At about 2.5x there are too few confident calls, auto falls back to IBS, and IBS still finds the clones but can merge close relatives: check the borderline joins.

The cut. Technical replicates are known clones, so they show how different two libraries of one genotype can look. CLONE_CUT = auto places the cut:

  • for genotype distance, at the bottom of the widest gap between joins that starts within three times the replicates' largest distance (clones sit just above the replicates; relatives are much further up);
  • for IBS, at the deepest join within any replicate set times TREE_BUFFER (1.10), the method of treeTrimmer.

gap or replicates forces one rule; a number sets the cut yourself (in the units of the distance used, given in <SP>CloneMetric.txt).

The run pauses after drawing angsd/<SP>CloneDend.pdf: the tree, technical replicates in bold, and the cut as a red line (with genotype distance, <SP>CloneDendIBS.pdf shows the IBS tree for comparison). Look for a gap between the clone-level pairs (replicates and true clones, near the bottom) and everything else. If the red line sits in that gap, accept it. If not, set your own.

nano popgen.config      # accept:  CLONE_PAUSE = no       or your own:  CLONE_CUT = 0.08
comrad run popgen

Checks that come with it:

  • Replicate check. <SP>CloneReplicates.txt gives each replicate's nearest sample and the nearest sample outside its set. A replicate whose nearest sample is outside its own clone group gives a WARNING: a mislabelled or failed library.
  • Borderline joins. <SP>CloneBorderline.txt lists joins grouped as clones but more than 1.5 times the replicates' distance, and the nearest join left ungrouped, with each side's coverage. A weak library on one side points to a clone; good coverage on both, to a close relative.
  • Too many clones. If the clone groups would drop more than CLONE_MAXDROP (half) of the samples, the run stops. That is a cut or data problem, not a result.
  • Clone-free check. After genotyping, the genotype step draws angsd/<SP>CloneFreeDend.pdf for the kept samples, with the same distance and cut, and warns about any pair still below it.

Replicates with no reads, or left out for low coverage, are warned about and left out; a replicate set needs two samples to count. If no set has two, set CLONE_CUT to a number.

docs.title: Pause 2: K
docs.text:
admix runs NGSadmix at every K from 1 to MAXK, ADMIX_REPS times each, and evalAdmix on the best run of each K. The K step then gives five reads on K, in the diary and in run/popgen/K.log:

note  K: evalAdmix elbow K = 2 (residual RMSD against K)
note  K: PCAngsd K = 2 (eigenvectors kept by its MAP test + 1; ...)
note  K: residual-block K = 2 (smallest K whose worst cluster-block mean |residual| < 0.01; plots: ngsAdmix/sintResiduals.pdf)
note  K: k-means BIC K = 2 (lowest BIC of k-means on the PCA scores, as adegenet find.clusters; table in ngsAdmix/sint_bic.txt)
note  K: runs in the dominant mode per K: 1:20/20 2:20/20 3:18/20 4:9/20
read what it is evalAdmix elbow where the residual curve flattens. A geometric rule: it always returns something, and never K = 1 or MAXK PCAngsd the number of eigenvectors PCAngsd's MAP test kept, plus one (Meisner & Albrechtsen 2018); its own admixture at that K is the bottom row of ngsAdmix/<SP>Admix.pdf k-means BIC k-means clustering of the PCA scores, K with the lowest BIC (the find.clusters step of DAPC; Jombart et al. 2010). Independent of NGSadmix. Like PCAngsd, it also answers to families and batches residual-block K from the evalAdmix residuals in ngsAdmix/<SP>Residuals.pdf. Each sample is placed in its main cluster at MAXK; a K that lumps two real lineages leaves positive residuals within them. This is the smallest K with no block mean above RESID_MAX. It cannot tell you K is too high, and the cut-off is a judgement call: look at the plots mode support how many of the NGSadmix runs agree at each K. Low support means that K is not a stable solution 
nano popgen.config      # K = 2
comrad run popgen

K = 1 (no structure) is allowed: every sample is one lineage, FST between lineages is skipped (FST among sampling groups still runs), and demography does not apply. At K ≥ 2, the run stops at assign if fewer than two lineages have pure samples, or any has fewer than MINPURE.

docs.title: After K
docs.text:
• Lineages. Each sample with at least ASSIGN (0.90) ancestry from one cluster belongs to that lineage; the rest are Admixed and stay out of the per-lineage statistics.
  • Kin. NGSremix estimates relatedness; for each pair at or above KIN (0.125), one sample is dropped: the one in most remaining pairs, then the one with less coverage.
  • Outliers. A PCAngsd selection scan within each lineage; SNPs with FDR < 0.05 on any PC are outliers, and their tags are removed from the SFS.
  • Neutral check. Structure is rerun without outliers or kin: PCAngsd, and NGSadmix with evalAdmix at every K from 1 to MAXK, with the same reads on K as at the pause (ngsAdmix/<SP>NeutralAdmix.pdf, <SP>NeutralResiduals.pdf). Close kin can pull PCs and clusters of their own and leave residual blocks, so this is K without them. If none of the elbow, PCAngsd, residual-block and k-means BIC K gives the K you chose, that is a WARNING. The lineage calls at your K are then compared with the full run's; a mismatch is a WARNING too, with the table in ngsAdmix/<SP>NeutralCompare.txt. Either way, change K and comrad from popgen assign if the kin-free run says otherwise.

docs.title: Demography
docs.text:
The demography pipeline fits two-population divergence models with moments to the 2D spectrum of every pair of lineages. It is an extra: run it in the species folder after popgen has finished, with K of at least 2.

comrad init demography
nano demography.config         # SP (as in popgen.config), MU
comrad check demography
comrad run demography

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
step does setup samples per lineage (demo/<SP>PopN.txt) and the lineage pairs boot contig-bootstrap 2D spectra for each pair: BOOT_JOBS jobs × BOOT_REPS replicates (100 by default) bootjoin joins the bootstrap spectra per pair moments every model in MODELS, FIT_SEEDS jobs × FIT_RUNS optimisations each (50 by default) collect the best run of each model, the model table, and the checks below tarball <SP>Demography.tar.gz and the HTML report

Models are ranked by CLAIC: AIC corrected for linked sites, from the bootstrap spectra, with Godambe standard errors for every parameter. MU (mutation rate per site per generation) converts the scaled parameters into individuals and generations.

docs.title: Models
docs.text: The names follow the usual convention: SI strict isolation, IM isolation with continuous migration, AM ancient migration (migration, then isolation), SC secondary contact (isolation, then migration). The suffix 2m adds heterogeneous migration across the genome, and 2N heterogeneous effective size; the ghost models add an unsampled population. momentsModels.py (see the scripts reference) fits them, and its source defines each one.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Convergence: do a model's best runs agree, across seeds? A model whose best fit came from only one seed is flagged in demo/<SP>Convergence.txt; give it more seeds before reading its parameters.
  • Nesting: every larger model should fit at least as well as the smaller model it contains. If one does not, its optimiser stopped early (demo/<SP>Nesting.txt).
  • Bounds and Godambe warnings from each kept run's log go in demo/<SP>Warnings.txt.

popgen decisions carry over: if kin or outliers were skipped there, the demography check warns, because the models assume unrelated samples and neutral sites.

docs.title: Popgen
docs.text:
The popgen pipeline takes one species from reads to lineages, kinship, diversity and FST. Run it from the species folder.

cd sint
comrad init popgen
nano popgen.config             # SP, GENOME_FASTA, META, TECHREPS, ... (the required lines are marked)
comrad check popgen
comrad run popgen

check confirms every program, file and metadata row is there, and prints the full options each step will run with. comrad list popgen shows which steps are done.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
stage step does Reads and mapping cutadapt quality-trims each sample readcounts counts reads per sample map bowtie2 to the host and, if given, the symbiont metagenome alignrates alignment-rate tables split keeps each read in host or symbiont, dropping reads that map to both; sorts and indexes bams/<s>.bam clean removes the raw mapping files; writes the bam lists QC and clones depth ANGSD depth pass and plotQC.py: each sample's proportion of sites at 3, 5, 10 and QDEPTHx clones ANGSD IBS and genotype calls on all samples, near-empty ones left out clonegroups clone distance (genotype or IBS) and cut from technical replicates, clone groups, dendrogram. Pause 1 filterbams keeps the best-covered sample of each clone group; drops samples below MINQ Genotypes and structure paralog ngsParalog: removes sites that look like collapsed paralogs genotype genotype likelihoods at SNPs in all kept samples; coverage at those SNPs per sample; clone-free check structure one SNP per tag; PCAngsd PCA and per-sample inbreeding admix NGSadmix at K = 1 to MAXK, ADMIX_REPS runs each; evalAdmix fit and residuals symbionts reads per symbiont genus (host-only runs skip it) K lays out the evidence for K. Pause 2 Lineages assign assigns each sample to a lineage if its ancestry is at least ASSIGN, otherwise Admixed kin NGSremix; drops one of each pair related at or above KIN (KIN_DROP = no: plots kinship but keeps everyone) lineagebams pure, kin-free samples per lineage lineagesnps SNPs within each lineage, with heterozygosity per site (LINEAGE_MAXHET); PCAngsd selection scan outliers outlier SNPs (FDR < 0.05 on any PC, per lineage); within-lineage PCA without them neutral reruns structure without outliers or kin and compares the lineage calls Statistics sfssites sites that pass the filters in every lineage, outlier tags removed saf site allele frequencies per lineage fst 2D spectra and FST between lineages, on those neutral sites fstall the same on the full panel, outliers in, for comparison groups FST among sampling groups within each lineage; π, θW, Tajima's D per group het heterozygosity per sample, every sample on the same sites theta π, Watterson's θ and Tajima's D per lineage, every lineage on the same sites tarball the results tarball and the HTML report

The two pauses are explained in Clones and K, and the outputs in Results.

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
MIN_IND (0.75) is the proportion of samples a site must have data in, for every ANGSD analysis; a section's min_ind overrides it. The depth pass uses 0.5.

Every ANGSD step reads with -minMapQ 20 -minQ 25. With 2bRAD's short tags, each mismatch to the reference lowers a read's mapping quality, so a stricter -minMapQ drops reads that carry the non-reference allele more often than reads that match, and heterozygotes look homozygous (on NWGOM data, MAPQ 30 kept 41-49% of one-mismatch reads against 70-73% of exact matches, and almost no two-mismatch reads). The sites for the SFS, θ, FST and heterozygosity use only filters that do not change allele frequencies: no -snp_pval, -minMaf or -hwe_pval, so invariant sites and rare variants stay in.

No step has a per-sample depth floor except heterozygosity (10 reads). The others pool genotype likelihoods across samples, which handles low depth; one sample on its own cannot. To add a floor for a sensitivity run, it is one line in that step's section:

[genotype]
args = -setMinDepthInd 3

Each section's args lists changes to the defaults, which init writes above it as a comment. comrad defaults popgen prints them all, and the settings reference lists every step's defaults.

docs.title: Leaving analyses out
docs.text:
SKIP lists steps not to run, e.g. SKIP = het theta groups. Only het theta groups fstall symbionts neutral kin outliers fst can be skipped. check says what each one changes, as a note or a WARNING, and stops on any step a later one needs:

note: SKIP het: no per-individual heterozygosity
WARNING: SKIP kin: related individuals stay in: SFS, theta, Tajima's D and FST will include close kin, ...
WARNING: SKIP outliers: SNPs under selection stay in the SFS and FST: demography assumes neutral sites, ...

A skipped step's files stay out of the results tarball. To run it later, take it out of SKIP and run comrad from popgen <step>.

docs.title: File names along the way
docs.text: demuxReads/<s>.demux.fastq.gz → filteredReads/<s>.filtered.fastq.gz (cutadapt) → filteredReads/<s>.host.bam and <s>.symbiont.bam (bowtie2, removed by clean) → bams/<s>.bam and bams/<s>.sym.bam. Analysis files start with SP (sintClones.ibsMat), logs are in each folder's logs/, and job lists are <SP><Step>Jobs.

docs.title: Plots
docs.text: Each step draws quick-look plots of what it made; Results, plots and the report lists them and how to set their colours and order.

docs.title: Reads
docs.text:
The reads pipeline turns raw pool fastqs into one file of clean, deduplicated reads per sample, sorted into a folder per species. Run it from the project folder.

comrad init reads
nano reads.config              # SAMPLE_SHEET, SPECIES (and BS_PROJECTS to download)
comrad check reads
comrad run reads

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
step does download downloads the pools from BaseSpace into rawReads/ (skipped when BS_PROJECTS is empty) demux trim2bRAD.py, one job per pool: finds the 2bRAD tag, removes PCR duplicates, and writes one file per in-line barcode, <pool>_<barcode>.demux.fastq.gz demuxcheck writes rawReads/RawCounts (raw and kept reads per pool), and stops if a pool kept less than MIN_KEPT percent rename sampleRename.py renames each library from the sample sheet, after a dry run that changes nothing if anything is wrong species moves each species' files into <species>/demuxReads/

A barcode with fewer than 100,000 reads (the trim2bRAD.py default) gets no file, so failed libraries are simply absent. To find a missing sample, look up its barcode in rawReads/logs/<pool>.demux.log.

Libraries with no sample name

A library missing from the sample sheet keeps its <pool>_<barcode> name, and the species step stops if any file matches no prefix in SPECIES. Add a catch-all for your pool names, e.g. unassigned=FG for pools named FG..., to collect them in their own folder.

docs.title: Checking the result
docs.text:
cat rawReads/RawCounts                            # raw and kept reads per pool
ls sint/demuxReads/*.demux.fastq.gz | wc -l       # samples per species
ls unassigned/demuxReads/                         # empty wells, barcode errors, unnamed libraries

docs.title: Starting from your own reads
docs.text: popgen only needs <species>/demuxReads/<sample>.demux.fastq.gz, one per sample. If your reads were demultiplexed elsewhere, put them there under those names and skip reads. Reads that are already quality-filtered can go in as filteredReads/<sample>.filtered.fastq.gz; see Running and rerunning.

docs.title: Results, plots and the report
docs.text:
When popgen finishes, the species folder holds <SP>Results.tar.gz: everything an analysis in R or Python needs, without the bams and intermediate files.

folder holds . bam lists, lineage calls (<SP>BamsClusters), sampling groups, kin table, alignment and retention rates, read counts qc depth distributions, each sample's proportion of sites at 3, 5, 10 and QDEPTHx clones clone groups, distance used and cut, dendrogram(s), replicate check, borderline joins, samples left out of the clone step structure beagle, PCAngsd covariance and inbreeding, best NGSadmix Q per K, evalAdmix fit and residuals, neutral rerun and its comparison with the lineages, outlier scans plots quick-look PDFs from each step (reads, symbionts, PCA, admixture, kinship, outliers, neutral run, FST, heterozygosity, θ); also inline in the report relatedness NGSremix table diversity heterozygosity, π/θ/Tajima's D, FST between lineages and among groups, 2D spectra run the diary, the report, tool versions and every copy of the settings

docs.title: Plots
docs.text:
Each step draws quick-look plots of what it made (plotStep.py), one PDF per step. They are for a first look; final figures belong in R. A plot that fails gives a WARNING and never stops the run.

step file shows alignrates filteredReads/<SP>Reads.pdf reads per sample; host and symbiont alignment rates symbionts bams/<SP>Symbionts.pdf share of symbiont reads per genus, per sample structure pcangsd/<SP>Pca.pdf PCA, PC1–2 and PC3–4, % variance on the axes admix ngsAdmix/<SP>Admix.pdf the clone-free tree with sampling-group tiles and admixture bars for K = 2…MAXK (and PCAngsd's K) in the tree's leaf order; the same bars ordered by sampling group; evalAdmix fit, likelihood and k-means BIC against K kin relatedness/<SP>Kin.pdf kinship by pair type (within each lineage, between lineages, with Admixed): histograms, boxplots of every pair and of each sample's closest relative, the share of pairs at or above each kinship, and counts per degree class; KIN and the KING degree bounds marked outliers angsd/lineages/<SP>Outliers.pdf selection statistic along the genome per lineage, outliers in red; within-lineage PCAs neutral ngsAdmix/<SP>Neutral.pdf, ngsAdmix/<SP>NeutralAdmix.pdf, pcangsd/<SP>PcaCompare.pdf neutral, kin-free bars beside the full run's at K; the kin-free admixture for every K; the PCA of all samples and the neutral, kin-free PCA, each coloured by sampling group and by lineage fst, fstall, groups sfs/<SP>Fst.pdf FST heatmaps on one colour scale: between lineages (neutral and all sites), between groups within lineages het het/<SP>Het.pdf heterozygosity per sample by lineage and by group; against coverage theta theta/<SP>Theta.pdf π, θW and Tajima's D per lineage (and the THETA_N subsample), and per sampling group reads pipeline rawReads/RawCounts.pdf raw and kept reads per pool

The clone dendrograms (angsd/clones/<SP>CloneDend.pdf, and angsd/<SP>CloneFreeDend.pdf from genotype) and the depth plots (angsd/<SP>Depth.pdf) come from their own steps.

A rerun never overwrites a plot: it writes <name>_v2.pdf, then _v3, and so on. The report shows the newest; the tarball's plots/ folder has them all.

docs.title: Colours, shapes and order
docs.text:
Samples are grouped along bar plots by META_GROUPS (or PLOT_ORDER); points are coloured by the first group column and shaped by the second (or PLOT_COLOR, PLOT_SHAPE). PLOT_LEVELS, PLOT_COLORS and PLOT_SHAPES set level order, colours and shapes per factor; a factor is a metadata column named in the config, or lineage:

PLOT_COLOR = depthZone
PLOT_SHAPE = bank
PLOT_LEVELS = bank: WFGB EFGB Bright McGrail; depthZone: Shallow Meso; lineage: Of1 Of2
PLOT_COLORS = depthZone: Shallow=f4a582 Meso=0571b0; lineage: Of1=red Of2=1b9e77
PLOT_SHAPES = bank: WFGB=o EFGB=^ Bright=s McGrail=D
PLOT_KCOLOR = 7570B3

PLOT_KCOLOR colours the admixture clusters from one colour toward white in MAXK steps, so each cluster keeps its colour in every K panel.

Colours are hex without the # (the config treats # as a comment) or names. comrad check stops on a factor that is not a metadata column and warns about levels it cannot find.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
run/popgen/popgenReport.html (also in the tarball) is one page per run:

  • Read first: every warning, and any pause or stop still open.
  • Samples: lineage sizes, samples left out of the clone step, the replicate check, clone groups, kin dropped, coverage per sample.
  • Structure: the K evidence, NGSadmix fit, the neutral comparison, inbreeding.
  • Differentiation and diversity: FST, θ, heterozygosity.
  • Plots: every step's quick-look plots, inline.
  • Settings, tool versions and the full diary.

comrad report popgen writes it at any point, including on a paused or stopped run.

docs.title: Diversity
docs.text:
Heterozygosity is estimated per sample, variant and invariant sites together (het/<SP>.het; means per lineage in <SP>Ho.txt): each sample on the SFS sites where it has at least 10 reads (the [het] -setMinDepthInd), as in Matz's 2bRAD scripts. het then tests whether heterozygosity follows coverage: Spearman's ρ with a permutation p, and the R² of a straight-line fit, against the number of sites and the proportion of sites at QDEPTHx (het/<SP>HetDepth.txt, the diary and the plot). A p below 0.05 is a WARNING: a sample with less coverage reaches 10 reads at fewer, and different, sites. Then set HET_DEPTH: every sample's reads are thinned at random (fixed seed) to that mean depth over the SFS sites before scoring, so all samples are scored at one depth, and samples below it are left out (angsd/<SP>HetExcluded; mean depths in het/<SP>HetMeanDepth.txt). Pick the highest depth that keeps most samples, with a floor of about 5 (-setMinDepthInd 5 in [het] args), and rerun het. Heterozygosity from 2bRAD reads is lower than the truth (allele dropout, low depth and the mapping-quality filter all hide heterozygotes), so compare samples and groups, not absolute values across studies.

θ. theta/<SP>Theta.out gives π, Watterson's θ, Tajima's D and the number of sites per lineage, from all its pure, kin-free samples (n), all lineages on the same sites (those in every lineage's SAF, theta/<SP>ThetaSites). π compares well between lineages of different size; θW and Tajima's D depend on n. With THETA_N set (a number, or min for the smallest lineage's n), the same statistics are also estimated from that many samples per lineage, in the Sub columns. The samples used are listed in theta/sub/ and are the same on every run. Compare θW and Tajima's D in those columns when lineage sizes differ much.

Sampling groups. groups estimates FST among sampling groups (the combination of META_GROUPS columns) within each lineage, for groups with at least MIN_GROUP (5) samples; the diary names each group left out and its n. It also gives π, θW and Tajima's D per group (angsd/groups/<SP>GroupTheta.out), every group on the same sites, from all its samples and from the smallest group's n (Sub columns: compare θW and Tajima's D there). With K = 1 this is the main diversity comparison. Heterozygosity per group is het/<SP>.het joined with angsd/<SP>Groups.

docs.title: F<sub>ST</sub>
docs.text: sfs/<SP>LineageFst.out has unweighted and weighted FST for each pair of lineages, on sites outside the outlier tags (realSFS -whichFst 1: Hudson's estimator as in Bhatia et al. 2013). sfs/<SP>LineageFstAll.out has the same on every site, outliers in, so you can see how much the outliers add.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
comrad run <pipeline> submits one small driver job that runs the pipeline's steps in order. Each step builds a list of jobs and hands it to comrad-jobs, which:

  • skips every job whose output is already there, so a rerun only does what is missing;
  • submits the rest as one SLURM job array, at most max_running tasks at once;
  • reruns only what fails: on long_queue after a time limit, with double the memory (up to max_mem) after running out, on another node after a node failure, and once more for anything else;
  • records what each job list used, in the diary.

A step ends in one of four ways:

outcome means what to do done finished nothing skip does not apply (no symbiont genome, in SKIP, ...) nothing pause a decision is needed: the clone threshold or K answer it in the config, then comrad run again stop something a rerun will not fix read the reason, fix it, then comrad run again

Problems that do not need to stop the run (replicates that don't group, samples with little coverage at the SNPs, a mismatch in the neutral check, heterozygosity that follows coverage) are WARNING lines in the diary and the report.

docs.title: Where it is, and why it stopped
docs.text:
comrad status popgen                 # the last events; the reason for a pause or stop is the last line
comrad list popgen                   # every step, done or pending
less run/popgen/<step>.log           # one step's full output
ls -t <folder>/<jobname>*.e* | head  # the jobs' own error files
comrad report popgen                 # run/popgen/popgenReport.html: warnings first, then the key tables
comrad summary popgen --dir mcav ofav sint   # from the project folder: each step's notes and warnings, and what waits on you
message usually means missing or empty: <file> an earlier step's output is gone; comrad from that step <n> samples ... no row in META add the rows to the metadata a spectrum did not converge a realSFS fit hit its iteration cap; see the CHECK lines in the step log clone grouping would drop ... the clone threshold is too high, or the samples are near-empty; set CLONE_CUT a lineage has fewer than MINPURE pure individuals K is too high, or ASSIGN too strict not on PATH: ... a program is missing; see Install

docs.title: Rerunning
docs.text:
you want to run carry on after a pause or a stop comrad run popgen redo from a step, because its inputs or settings changed comrad from popgen <step> start at a step, because the earlier ones were done another way comrad from popgen <step> --mark-earlier run one step now, in this shell comrad step popgen <step> run the whole thing in this shell instead of a driver job comrad run popgen --here

run skips steps that are done, and within a step, jobs that are done. It does not notice files you changed by hand, or a new setting for a step that has already run: that is what from is for. Every job in a rewound step reruns, even where an old output exists.

A driver stopped by its time limit loses nothing; comrad run picks up at the step it was in. Don't move a species folder while its driver is running (paths are absolute); move it between runs.

docs.title: Starting part way
docs.text:
If the reads were already quality-filtered, put them in filteredReads/<sample>.filtered.fastq.gz with a read-count table filteredReads/<SP>ReadCounts (readCounts.py -f filtered.fastq.gz -o <SP>Read), then start at mapping:

comrad check popgen && comrad from popgen map --mark-earlier

docs.title: Jobs, logs and memory
docs.text:
Every job list has its own section in the config, which init writes with its defaults:

[map]                    # bowtie2, one job per sample (host and symbiont)
cpus = 1
mem =                    # empty = the bowtie2 index size x 1.5 + 2 GB
# default args: --no-unal --score-min L,16,1 --local -L 16
args =                   # changes only

[admix]                  # NGSadmix, one job per K and replicate
cpus = 10
mem = 8GB
  • cpus is both what SLURM reserves and the tool's own thread count (-P, --threads, -p): a reservation alone does not make a program use the cores.
  • mem is per task. A task that runs out is resubmitted with double, up to max_mem, so a low figure costs a retry, not the run. If tasks keep running out, raise it.
  • queue = long sends that job list straight to long_queue, and slurm = constraint=amd adds --constraint=amd to its jobs. In cluster.config, slurm applies to every job.
  • No time limit is asked for unless you set one, so each task gets its partition's own.

Each job list's logs are combined into one pair next to its outputs when the array ends: a summary table with failed tasks first, then a section per task with its node, exit code and run time. The diary notes what each job list used:

note  map: sintHostMap: 128 jobs, peak 3.1 GB of 6GB, longest 0.68 h, 61.2 CPU-hours

docs.title: What gets recorded
docs.text:
file holds run/<pipeline>/<pipeline>Summary.txt the diary: every submit, step start and finish, note lines with the numbers for your methods (samples kept, SNPs, clone threshold, K evidence, kin dropped, FST, best model), warnings, pauses and stops run/<pipeline>/versions.txt comRAD, Python and its packages, every program's version (or path and checksum, when it has no version flag), every script's checksum, the loaded modules run/<pipeline>/<pipeline>.config.<date> every setting in effect, saved whenever one changes run/<pipeline>/<step>.log each step's full output run/<pipeline>/<pipeline>Report.html the report

All of these go in the results tarball.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A Linux cluster with SLURM. comRAD submits job arrays; nothing else is needed for submitting.
  • comRAD and the programs it runs: see Install. comrad check <pipeline> lists anything missing.
  • Reference genomes, indexed once:
bowtie2-build sintGenome.fa sintGenome.fa && samtools faidx sintGenome.fa

For a host/symbiont system you also need a symbiont metagenome (indexed the same way) and a two-column table of its chromosomes and their genus (chromosome<TAB>genus), for the symbiont read counts. packMetagenome.py packs several symbiont genomes into one metagenome with each chromosome named after its genome (Sym001, Brev001, ...), which makes that table a one-line job.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
file what it holds rawReads/<pool>.fastq.gz one fastq per pool (one Illumina index), named by pool. Downloaded for you from BaseSpace if you give BS_PROJECTS sampleID.csv one line per library, no header: <pool>_<barcode>,<sample> metadata.csv one row per sample, replicates included: a sample column plus whatever you group by (bank, depthZone, ...)

Filled-in examples of each are in examples/.

docs.title: Naming conventions
docs.text:
comRAD relies on a few naming rules:

  • Sample names are the bam file names without .bam, and the values in the metadata's sample column (META_SAMPLE). Every sample with reads needs a metadata row; comrad check popgen lists any that don't have one.
  • Technical replicates are <sample>.1, <sample>.2, ..., with the original library as .1. They set the clone threshold, so name them this way and list them in TECHREPS.
  • Species are told apart by sample-name prefix (SPECIES = mcav=MGM ofav=OGM): every sample starting MGM goes to the mcav folder.

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
myProject/                    cluster.config  reads.config  sampleID.csv  metadata.csv  rawReads/
  sint/                       popgen.config  demography.config
    demuxReads/ filteredReads/ bams/ angsd/ pcangsd/ ngsAdmix/ relatedness/ sfs/ het/ theta/ demo/
    run/popgen/               a .log and .done per step, the diary, versions, settings copies
  past/                       ...

Each pipeline runs from the folder it works in: reads from the project folder, popgen and demography from a species folder. Paths in a config can be absolute, relative to that folder, or use any exported variable ($STORAGE/genomes/sint.fa).

docs.title: Cluster settings
docs.text:
Once per project, in the project folder:

comrad init cluster
nano cluster.config
setting set it to queue the partition jobs start on long_queue the partition for jobs that run out of time (empty: they stop instead) max_mem your largest node's memory; out-of-memory retries double up to this email where SLURM mails failures and the end of a pipeline slurm extra sbatch flags every job needs, e.g. account=mylab constraint=amd

sinfo -o "%P %m %l" lists the partitions, their node memory (MB) and time limits. Every pipeline run in this folder, or up to three folders below it, reads this file. All settings are listed in the settings reference.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Two commands: comrad, which runs the pipelines, and comrad-jobs, which submits and watches job lists (the pipelines call it; it also works on its own). Below is each one's --help, as tools/makeDocs.py captured it.

docs.title: comrad
docs.text:
usage: comrad [-h] command ...

Run a comRAD pipeline from the folder it works in.

Pipelines:
  reads        project folder: download, trim and demultiplex, rename, split by species
  popgen       species folder: QC, mapping, clones, genotyping, structure, K, kin,
               lineages, outliers, SFS, FST, diversity, results tarball
  demography   species folder, after popgen: bootstrap SFS, moments, results tarball

Each pipeline reads <pipeline>.config in the current folder (`init` writes one to
fill in), after cluster.config (partitions, memory limit, email, extra sbatch
flags) from this folder or up to three above it (`init cluster` writes one).
Every job list has its own [section] in the config: cpus, mem, queue, slurm and
the tool's own options. State is kept in run/<pipeline>/: a .done marker and a
.log per step, and <pipeline>Summary.txt with one line per event. `run` submits
one small driver job (no time limit given) that runs the steps in order.
Steps submit their own jobs through comrad-jobs, which reruns failed jobs by
itself; a step stops the run only when something is wrong that a rerun would
not fix, and pauses it where a decision is needed (K). Submitting again picks
up after the last finished step.

positional arguments:
  command
    setup     find or install the tools the pipelines run
    defaults  print every default setting of a pipeline
    init      write <pipeline>.config (or cluster.config) to fill in
    check     check <pipeline>.config and its inputs
    run       submit the driver job
    status    last events, and whether the driver is queued
    list      every step, done or pending
    from      clear the done markers from STEP on, then submit
    step      run one step now, in this shell
    report    write run/<pipeline>/<pipeline>Report.html: warnings, pauses and stops, then the key
              tables
    summary   print open pauses and stops, then each step's notes and warnings from its last run

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

examples:
  cd /path/to/myProject
  comrad init cluster               # writes cluster.config (partitions, memory, email); once per project
  comrad init reads                 # writes reads.config; fill it in
  comrad check reads                # is everything it names there?
  comrad run reads                  # submit; species folders appear when it finishes

  cd /path/to/myProject/sint
  comrad init popgen && nano popgen.config
  comrad run popgen                 # pauses at K
  comrad status popgen              # where it is, or why it stopped
  nano popgen.config && comrad run popgen   # K = 2 in the config
  comrad from popgen clonegroups    # forget that step and everything after, resubmit
  comrad from popgen kin --mark-earlier --no-submit   # earlier steps were run by hand
  comrad step popgen fst            # run one step now, in this shell
  comrad list demography            # the steps, done or pending
  comrad report popgen              # run/popgen/popgenReport.html: warnings first, then the key tables
  comrad summary popgen --dir mcav ofav sint past   # from the project folder: what each step said, and what is waiting on you
  comrad setup --prefix /path/to/bin/comradDeps   # find or install the external tools
